questiontext.text: In a strict layered architecture, each layer may use which other layer?

answer.text: Only the layer directly below it

feedback.text: Correct — dependencies point downward, one level.
No — dependencies go downward, not upward.
That would break layering.
A strict layer uses the one directly below, not always the bottom.

generalfeedback.text: A strict layered architecture allows a layer to depend only on the layer immediately beneath it, keeping dependencies unidirectional.

questiontext.text: Which ordering shows a typical top-to-bottom layering?

feedback.text: Correct — UI on top, data access at the bottom.
That ordering is not the conventional layering.
Presentation is normally the top layer.

answer.text: Data-access → Business → Presentation is used top-down

feedback.text: That is bottom-up; top-down is Presentation first.

generalfeedback.text: A common three-tier stack is Presentation on top, Business logic in the middle, and Data-access at the bottom.

questiontext.text: What is the main goal of organizing a system into layers?

feedback.text: Correct — each layer has a focused responsibility.
Not a goal — that harms maintainability.
Layers rely on interfaces between them.
Unrelated to layering.

generalfeedback.text: Layering separates concerns so each layer can be developed, understood, and replaced independently.

questiontext.text: A layered architecture is also commonly called ______.

feedback.text: Correct.
P2P is a different style with no fixed layers.
Event-driven is a separate style.
Layering is not defined by being monolithic.

generalfeedback.text: Layered architectures are frequently described as n-tier (e.g., 3-tier: presentation, business, data).

questiontext.text: Which statements about layered architecture are true? (select all that apply)

feedback.text: Yes.

answer.text: Higher layers depend on lower layers, not the reverse

feedback.text: Yes — dependencies flow downward.

answer.text: A lower layer should call directly into the presentation layer

feedback.text: No — that reverses the dependency direction.

answer.text: Every layer may freely depend on every other layer

feedback.text: No — strict layering restricts this.

generalfeedback.text: Layered architecture separates concerns with downward, restricted dependencies (often described as n-tier).

questiontext.text: In a strict layered architecture, dependencies flow downward: a layer uses the layer beneath it.

feedback.text: Correct — that unidirectional rule defines strict layering.
Downward, unidirectional dependency is the defining rule.

questiontext.text: Strict layering allows the data-access layer to call directly into the presentation layer.

feedback.text: No — that violates the downward dependency rule.
Correct — lower layers do not call up into presentation.

questiontext.text: In this architectural style the system is divided into stacked ______s, each using only the one below it. (one word, English, singular)

feedback.text: Correct.
Correct.
Accepted — n-tier is the common synonym.
